title: Workforce access: Azure RBAC vs IAM Identity Center
summary: How people get access to cloud resources. Both bind a group to a set of permissions at a place, but Azure binds directly at any scope in a tree, while AWS binds per account and provisions a role in each one.

dimensions.label: Sign-in
values: Identity Center, often federated with a corporate IdP

dimensions.label: Where it applies
values: Any scope: management group, subscription, resource group, resource

dimensions.label: Inheritance
values: None between accounts; one assignment per account

dimensions.label: What the person gets
values: Their own token; no separate identity
A session as a provisioned IAM role (AWSReservedSSO_…)

dimensions.label: Just-in-time access
values: Not built in; temporary assignments or partner tools

notes: Both work best with groups from the corporate IdP: joiners and leavers then only change the IdP group.
Azure can grant at resource-group or resource level directly. In AWS, finer-grained limits go into the permission set's policies or into separate accounts.
